questions.prompt: Do you think it is important to learn about history?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. History good. I like history. It's about old things.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I think history is important. It is about the past. We can learn about kings and queens and wars. And it is interesting to know what happened before.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I think it's important to learn about history. It helps us understand the present. For example, we can learn about why some countries are rich and others are poor. Also, it's interesting to know about famous people and events from the past.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, yes, I think it's really important. History helps us make sense of the world we live in today. When you look into past mistakes and conflicts, you start to understand why things turned out the way they did. I suppose it also gives you a much stronger sense of where you come from.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Tarix yaxshi. Menga tarix yoqadi. Bu eski narsalar haqida.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menimcha tarix muhim. Bu o'tmish haqida. Biz qirollar va malikalar va urushlar haqida bilib olishimiz mumkin. Va avval nima bo'lganini bilish qiziq.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, menimcha tarixni o'rganish muhim. Bu bizga hozirgi zamonni tushunishga yordam beradi.
Masalan, nega ba'zi davlatlar boy, boshqalari esa kambag'al ekanligini bilib olishimiz mumkin. Bundan tashqari, o'tmishdagi mashhur odamlar va voqealar haqida bilish qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men tarixni o'rganish muhim deb hisoblayman. U hozirgi voqealar uchun kontekst yaratadi va bizga zamonaviy dunyoning murakkabliklarini tushunishga imkon beradi. O'tmishdagi mojarolar va ijtimoiy o'zgarishlarni o'rganish orqali biz inson xulq-atvori va harakatlarimizning potentsial oqibatlari haqida qimmatli tushunchalarga ega bo'lishimiz mumkin. Bundan tashqari, tarixni bilish madaniy o'zlik tuyg'usini shakllantiradi va bizga o'tmishda yashaganlarning yutuqlari va kurashlarini qadrlashga imkon beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you think it is important to learn about history?
idioms: Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it - "O'tmishni eslab qololmaganlar uni takrorlashga mahkum"
history repeats itself - "tarix takrorlanadi"
turn over a new leaf - "yangi sahifani ochmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I strongly believe that learning about history is..." - "Ha, men tarixni o'rganish ... deb qat'iy ishonaman"
"By studying history, we can learn from..." - "Tarixni o'rganish orqali biz ... dan saboq olishimiz mumkin"
"Furthermore, history teaches us..." - "Bundan tashqari, tarix bizga ... o'rgatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I strongly believe that learning about history is extremely important. It helps us understand how our society has evolved and why things are the way they are today.
By studying history, we can learn from the mistakes of previous generations and avoid repeating them. It also gives us a deeper appreciation of our cultural heritage and national identity.
Furthermore, history teaches us critical thinking — we learn to analyse events, question sources, and form our own opinions. As they say, "Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men tarixni o'rganish juda muhim deb hisoblayman. Bu bizning jamiyatimiz qanday rivojlanganini va narsalar nega bugungi kundagidek ekanligini tushunishga yordam beradi.

Tarixni o'rganish orqali biz avvalgi avlodlarning xatolaridan saboq olishimiz va ularni takrorlashdan qochishimiz mumkin. Shuningdek, u bizga madaniy merosimiz va milliy o'zligimizni chuqurroq anglash imkonini beradi.

Bundan tashqari, tarix bizga tanqidiy fikrlashni o'rgatadi — biz voqealarni tahlil qilishni, manbalarni so'roq qilishni va o'z fikrlarimizni shakllantirishni o'rganamiz. Aytishlaricha, "O'tmishni eslay olmaydiganlar uni takrorlashga mahkumdirlar".

questions.prompt: Have you ever taken part in a cultural festival or event?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I went to a festival. It was good. Music.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I have. I went to a festival last year. It was fun and I saw music. I ate food too, and it was good. I liked it.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I have taken part in a cultural event. Last year, I went to a food festival. It was interesting because I tried a lot of new foods. I think it's good to try new things from other cultures. Also, there was music and dancing.
questions.sampleB2: Yes, I actually have. A couple of years back I went to our local Navruz celebration, and it was a real eye-opener. The whole square was buzzing with traditional music and dancing, and everyone was dressed up in colourful costumes. If you ask me, though, the best part was tucking into all the homemade food — it really brought the community together.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men festivalga bordim. Yaxshi edi. Musiqa.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men qatnashganman. O'tgan yili bir festivalga borgan edim. U qiziqarli edi va men musiqa ko'rdim. Men ham ovqat yedim va u mazali edi. Menga yoqdi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Ha, men bir madaniy tadbirda ishtirok etganman. O'tgan yili men oziq-ovqat festivaliga borgan edim. Bu qiziqarli edi, chunki men ko'p yangi ovqatlarni tatib ko'rdim. Menimcha, boshqa madaniyatlardan yangi narsalarni sinab ko'rish yaxshi. Shuningdek, u yerda musiqa va raqs ham bor edi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, men bir nechta madaniy festivallarda ishtirok etganman. Bir necha yil oldin Diwali bayramiga borganim esimda. U juda ham yorqin edi, hamma joyda rang-barang chiroqlar va an'anaviy kiyimlar bor edi. Men uchun ayniqsa qiziqarli bo'lgan narsa, festivalning diniy ahamiyati haqida bilib olish bo'ldi. Bu menga boshqa nuqtai nazarni ko'rishga yordam berdi. Menimcha, bunday tadbirlar qimmatli, chunki ular turli madaniyatlarni tushunish va qadrlashga yordam beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Have you ever taken part in a cultural festival or event?
idioms: Culture is the widening of the mind and of the spirit - "Madaniyat - aql va ruhning kengayishi"
when in Rome, do as the Romans do - "Rimda bo'lsang, rimliklar qilganidek qil"
old habits die hard - "eski odatlar qiyin o'ladi"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I have! I actually took part in..." - "Ha, bor! Men aslida ... da qatnashganman"
"The festival was full of..." - "Festival ... ga to'la edi"
"I think cultural festivals are incredibly important because..." - "Menimcha, madaniy festivallar juda muhim, chunki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I have! I actually took part in our local Navruz celebration last year. It was an absolutely fantastic experience.
The festival was full of traditional music, dancing, and delicious food. I particularly enjoyed watching the folk performances and trying different homemade dishes that people had prepared. It was a wonderful way to connect with my roots.
I think cultural festivals are incredibly important because they bring communities together and help preserve traditions and customs that might otherwise be forgotten. As they say, "Culture is the widening of the mind and of the spirit".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men qatnashganman! Men o'tgan yili mahalliy Navro'z bayramida qatnashdim. Bu juda ajoyib tajriba edi.
Festival an'anaviy musiqa, raqslar va mazali taomlarga to'la edi. Men ayniqsa xalq ijrolarini tomosha qilishdan va odamlar tayyorlagan turli xil uy taomlarini tatib ko'rishdan zavq oldim. Bu o'z ildizlarim bilan bog'lanishning ajoyib usuli edi.
Menimcha, madaniy festivallar juda muhim, chunki ular jamiyatlarni birlashtiradi va aks holda unutilishi mumkin bo'lgan an'analar va urf-odatlarni saqlashga yordam beradi. Aytishlaricha, "Madaniyat - bu aql va ruhning kengayishidir".

questions.prompt: Do you prefer giving handmade gifts or buying ready-made ones?
questions.sampleA1: I like buy gifts. It is easy. I buy it at shop.
questions.sampleA2: I like to buy gifts. It's easier and faster. I can find many things in the shop. But sometimes I make gifts, and it is nice too.
questions.sampleB1: I think I prefer buying gifts. It's more convenient because I don't have a lot of free time. For example, if someone likes books, I can easily buy them a book. However, a handmade gift can be more personal, but it takes a lot of effort.
questions.sampleB2: Personally, I lean towards handmade gifts whenever I can manage it. The thing is, putting your own time and effort into something makes it far more personal and meaningful. Mind you, when I'm pushed for time, I'll happily buy something ready-made. At the end of the day, it's the thought that counts, not the price tag.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men sovg'alar sotib olishni yaxshi ko'raman. Bu oson. Men uni do'kondan sotib olaman.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men sovg'alar sotib olishni yoqtiraman. Bu osonroq va tezroq. Men do'konda ko'p narsalarni topishim mumkin.
Lekin ba'zida men sovg'alar yasayman, va bu ham yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, sovg'a sotib olganim ma'qul. Bu qulayroq, chunki menda bo'sh vaqt ko'p emas.
Masalan, agar kimdir kitoblarni yoqtirsa, men ularga osongina kitob sotib olishim mumkin.
Biroq, qo'lda yasalgan sovg'a shaxsiyroq bo'lishi mumkin, lekin bu ko'p mehnat talab qiladi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men tayyor sovg'alar sotib olishga moyilman, asosan vaqt cheklovlari tufayli. Noldan biror narsa yaratish vaqt va mahoratga katta sarmoya talab qiladi, bu esa menda ko'pincha yetishmaydi. Qo'lda yasalgan narsalar ortidagi his-tuyg'ularni qadrlamayman degani emas; aslida, men ularni juda o'ylab topilgan deb bilaman. Biroq, menimcha, yaxshi tanlangan, tayyor sovg'a ham xuddi shunday mazmunli bo'lishi mumkin, bu siz oluvchining didi va ehtiyojlarini tushunishingizni ko'rsatadi. Oxir oqibat, qadr-qimmat yaratilish jarayonida emas, balki niyatda.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you prefer giving handmade gifts or buying ready-made ones?
idioms: It's the thought that counts - "Muhimi - e'tibor"
from the bottom of my heart - "chin yurakdan"
give and take - "berish va olish"
sentenceStarters: "I generally prefer giving handmade gifts whenever..." - "Men odatda ... bo'lganda qo'lda yasalgan sovg'alarni berishni afzal ko'raman"
"For example, I once made a photo album for..." - "Masalan, men bir marta ... uchun fotoalbom yasadim"
"However, I must admit that when I'm short on time..." - "Biroq, tan olishim kerakki, vaqtim kam bo'lganda..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I generally prefer giving handmade gifts whenever I have the time and opportunity. There's something truly special about a gift that someone has put personal effort into creating.
For example, I once made a photo album for my best friend's birthday, filled with our favourite memories together. The personal touch made it much more meaningful than anything I could have bought from a shop. She was genuinely moved by it.
However, I must admit that when I'm short on time, I do resort to buying ready-made gifts. The most important thing is the thought behind the gift, not its price tag. As they say, "It's the thought that counts".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men, odatda, vaqtim va imkoniyatim bo'lganda, qo'lda yasalgan sovg'alar berishni afzal ko'raman. Kimdir shaxsiy mehnatini sarflab yaratgan sovg'ada o'zgacha bir narsa bor.

Misol uchun, bir marta eng yaqin do'stimning tug'ilgan kuniga fotoalbom yasaganman, ichiga birga o'tkazgan eng sevimli xotiralarimizni joylaganman. Shaxsiy yondashuv uni do'kondan sotib olishim mumkin bo'lgan har qanday narsadan ko'ra ancha mazmunli qildi. U bundan chin dildan ta'sirlandi.

Lekin, tan olishim kerakki, vaqtim kam bo'lganda, tayyor sovg'alar sotib olishga majbur bo'laman. Eng muhimi, sovg'aning narxi emas, balki uning ortidagi fikrdir. Aytishlaricha, "Muhimi - niyat".

questions.prompt: Describe what is happening in each photo.
questions.sampleA1:
Photo one, people clean. They have bags.

Photo two, people clean too. It is good.
questions.sampleA2:
In the first photo, people are cleaning the street. They have special clothes.

And in the second photo, other people are cleaning too, but they are different. I think they are friends.
questions.sampleB1:
The first picture shows people cleaning the street. They look like they are paid to do it, because they have uniforms.

The second picture also shows people cleaning, but it's different. They are probably volunteers. I think it's good that people help to clean.

Both pictures are about cleaning, but in different ways.
questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, I can see four professional gardeners hard at work in a beautiful, well-maintained garden. They're all men, dressed in uniforms, carrying out various tasks: power washing a path, raking, and tending to the plants and a pond. Moving on to the second image, it shows a group of four volunteers, two men and two women, picking up litter in what looks like a public park. They're wearing blue 'VOLUNTEER' T-shirts and putting plastic bottles into green bin bags. Overall, both photos depict people working outdoors, but the first highlights a paid service and skilled labour, whereas the second illustrates a community effort to keep public spaces clean.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Birinchi suratda odamlar tozalashyapti. Ularda xaltalar bor.

Ikkinchi suratda ham odamlar tozalashyapti. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Birinchi suratda odamlar ko'chani tozalashyapti. Ularning maxsus kiyimlari bor.

Va ikkinchi suratda ham boshqa odamlar tozalashyapti, lekin ular boshqacha. Menimcha, ular do'stlar.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda odamlar ko'chani tozalashayotgani ko'rsatilgan. Ularga pul to'lanayotganga o'xshaydi, chunki ularda formalar bor.

Ikkinchi rasmda ham odamlar tozalashayotgani ko'rsatilgan, lekin bu boshqacha. Ular ehtimol ko'ngillilardir. Odamlar tozalashga yordam berishlari yaxshi deb o'ylayman.

Ikkala rasm ham tozalash haqida, lekin har xil usullarda.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ikkala suratda ham odamlar atrof-muhitni tozalash bilan shug'ullanayotgani tasvirlangan, garchi turli xil sharoitlarda bo'lsa ham.

Birinchi surat professional tozalash guruhini aks ettirayotganga o'xshaydi. Ularning kiyimi va jihozlariga qarab, ular shu maqsadda yollangan bo'lishi mumkin, bu esa tizimli va ehtimol hukumat tomonidan boshqariladigan tashabbusni ko'rsatadi.

Aksincha, ikkinchi suratda ko'ngillilar guruhi mahalliy tozalash ishlarida ishtirok etayotgani ko'rsatilgan. Atmosfera yanada norasmiy va o'zlarining mahalliy muhitiga nisbatan umumiy mas'uliyat tuyg'usi bilan boshqariladiganga o'xshaydi. Birinchi surat tashkil etilgan mehnatni ta'kidlasa, ikkinchisi fuqarolik ishtiroki va jamoatchilik ruhini urg'ulaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - Describe what is happening in each photo
idioms: many hands make light work - "ko'p qo'l ishni yengillashtiradi"
actions speak louder than words - "amallar so'zlardan balandroq gapiradi"
give back to the community - "jamoaga qaytarmoq"
sentenceStarters: "These two photos show different approaches to..." - "Bu ikki rasm ... ga turli yondashuvlarni ko'rsatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
These two photos show different approaches to keeping our environment clean.
In the first photo, I can see a team of professional cleaners carrying out a clean-up operation. They appear to be wearing uniforms and using specialised equipment, which suggests this is a paid service. Everything looks very organised and efficiently managed.
The second photo presents a very different scene — a group of community volunteers working together to clean up their neighbourhood. They seem enthusiastic and motivated, doing this out of their own goodwill rather than for payment. The atmosphere looks much more collaborative and community-spirited.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki surat atrof-muhitimizni toza saqlashga turli yondashuvlarni ko'rsatadi.
Birinchi suratda men tozalash operatsiyasini amalga oshirayotgan professional tozalovchilar jamoasini ko'rishim mumkin. Ularning uniforma kiyganligi va maxsus uskunalar ishlatayotganligi, bu pullik xizmat ekanligini ko'rsatadi. Hamma narsa juda tartibli va samarali boshqarilganga o'xshaydi.
Ikkinchi surat juda boshqacha manzarani taqdim etadi — o'z mahallalarini tozalash uchun birgalikda ishlayotgan ko'ngillilar guruhi. Ular g'ayratli va rag'batlantirilganga o'xshaydi, buni to'lov uchun emas, balki o'z xohishlari bilan qilishmoqda. Atmosfera ancha hamkorlikka asoslangan va jamoaviy ruhda ekanligi ko'rinadi.

questions.prompt: What are the benefits of community volunteer actions like clean-up days?
questions.sampleA1: I like clean. Clean is good. Help clean park.
questions.sampleA2: It is good to help. We clean the street and the park. It's nice to clean and it's good for everyone.
questions.sampleB1: I think clean-up days are good. They help to make the community look nicer. Also, it's a good way to meet new people and work together. For example, we cleaned the park last year and it looked much better afterwards. I think it's important to help.
questions.sampleB2: Well, there are quite a few benefits. First off, they bring neighbours together and build a real sense of community. On top of that, clearing away litter obviously makes the area cleaner and more pleasant to live in. I suppose the biggest plus, though, is that it raises awareness about looking after our environment. Every little helps, after all.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga tozalik yoqadi. Tozalik yaxshi. Parkni tozalashga yordam berish.
questions.uzSampleA2: Yordam berish yaxshi. Biz ko'chani va parkni tozalaymiz. Tozalash yoqimli va bu hamma uchun foydali.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, tozalash kunlari yaxshi. Ular jamiyatning chiroyli ko'rinishiga yordam beradi. Shuningdek, bu yangi odamlar bilan tanishish va birgalikda ishlash uchun yaxshi usul.
Masalan, o'tgan yili biz parkni tozaladik va keyin u ancha yaxshi ko'rindi. Menimcha, yordam berish muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Mahalliy obodonlashtirish kunlari bir qancha afzalliklarni taqdim etadi. Birinchidan, ular, albatta, mahalliy hududning tashqi ko'rinishini yaxshilaydi va yashash uchun yanada yoqimli joyga aylantiradi. Ikkinchidan, bu kabi tadbirlar aholi o'rtasida jamoaviy ruh va hamkorlik tuyg'usini uyg'otadi. Odamlar umumiy maqsad sari birgalikda harakat qilishganda, ijtimoiy aloqalar mustahkamlanadi. Nihoyat, bu harakatlar atrof-muhit muammolari haqida xabardorlikni oshirishi va uzoq muddatda yanada barqaror xatti-harakatlarni rag'batlantirishi mumkin. Bu yaxshiroq atrof-muhitga hissa qo'shishning amaliy usuli.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the benefits of community volunteer actions like clean-up days?
idioms: No act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted - "Hech qanday yaxshilik, qanchalik kichik bo'lmasin, behuda ketmaydi"
it takes a village - "butun jamoa kerak"
charity begins at home - "xayriya uydan boshlanadi"
sentenceStarters: "Community volunteer actions offer numerous benefits that..." - "Jamoaviy ko'ngillilik tadbirlari ... dan tashqariga chiqadigan ko'plab foydalarga ega"
"Firstly, they create a strong sense of community..." - "Birinchidan, ular kuchli jamoaviylik hissini yaratadi..."
"Furthermore, volunteering teaches valuable life skills..." - "Bundan tashqari, ko'ngillilik qimmatli hayotiy ko'nikmalarni o'rgatadi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Community volunteer actions like clean-up days, as shown in the second photo, offer numerous benefits that go far beyond just tidying up the streets.
Firstly, they create a strong sense of community. When neighbours come together to work towards a common goal, it builds bonds and strengthens social connections. People get to know each other better and develop a shared sense of pride in their neighbourhood.
Secondly, volunteer clean-ups have a direct and visible positive impact on the local environment. Removing litter, planting trees, and cleaning public spaces make the area more pleasant and healthier for everyone. It also raises environmental awareness among participants and onlookers alike.
Furthermore, volunteering teaches valuable life skills such as teamwork, responsibility, and civic engagement. It's especially beneficial for young people who learn the importance of giving back. As they say, "No act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ikkinchi suratda ko'rsatilganidek, tozalash kunlari kabi jamoat ko'ngillilik harakatlari ko'chalarni shunchaki tartibga solishdan ko'ra ko'proq foyda keltiradi.

Birinchidan, ular kuchli jamoatchilik tuyg'usini yaratadi. Qo'shnilar umumiy maqsad sari birgalikda harakat qilsalar, bu aloqalarni mustahkamlaydi va ijtimoiy bog'lanishlarni kuchaytiradi. Odamlar bir-birlarini yaxshiroq bilishadi va o'z mahallalaridan faxrlanish tuyg'usini rivojlantiradilar.

Ikkinchidan, ko'ngillilar tomonidan tozalash ishlari mahalliy atrof-muhitga bevosita va ko'rinadigan ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatadi. Chiqindilarni olib tashlash, daraxtlar ekish va jamoat joylarini tozalash hududni hamma uchun yanada yoqimli va sog'lom qiladi. Shuningdek, bu ishtirokchilar va tomoshabinlar orasida atrof-muhit haqida xabardorlikni oshiradi.

Bundan tashqari, ko'ngillilik jamoada ishlash, mas'uliyat va fuqarolik faolligi kabi qimmatli hayotiy ko'nikmalarni o'rgatadi. Bu, ayniqsa, yoshlar uchun foydali, ular berishning muhimligini o'rganadilar. Aytishlaricha, "Hech qanday yaxshilik, hatto u qanchalik kichik bo'lmasin, hech qachon behuda ketmaydi".

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer paid services instead of doing things themselves?
questions.sampleA1: I think… because easy. I pay. Good.
questions.sampleA2: Some people pay. Because it's easy. And they don't have time. I like to do it myself, but sometimes it's hard.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think some people prefer to pay for services because it's more convenient. For example, if you are busy with work, it's easier to pay someone to clean your house. Also, they might not know how to do it themselves, so it's better to pay someone who does.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I think it mostly comes down to time. A lot of people are run off their feet with work and family, so paying someone to handle a chore frees them up. Besides, professionals usually do a neater job, so you get real value for money. And let's face it, some jobs are just too tricky to tackle on your own.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men o'ylayman... chunki oson. Men to'layman. Yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ba'zi odamlar pul to'laydi. Chunki bu oson. Va ularning vaqti yo'q. Men o'zim qilishni yaxshi ko'raman, lekin ba'zida bu qiyin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, ba'zi odamlar xizmatlar uchun pul to'lashni afzal ko'rishadi, chunki bu qulayroq.
Masalan, agar siz ish bilan band bo'lsangiz, uyingizni tozalash uchun kimdirga pul to'lash osonroq.
Shuningdek, ular buni qanday qilishni bilmasligi mumkin, shuning uchun buni uddalaydigan odamga pul to'lash yaxshiroq.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Odamlarning o'zlari qilish o'rniga pullik xizmatlarni tanlashining bir nechta sababi bor.
Birinchidan, qulaylik katta omil. Ko'p odamlar band hayot kechirishadi va tozalash yoki uy ta'miri kabi vazifalarga vaqt ajratishga shunchaki vaqtlari yo'q.
Ikkinchidan, tajriba muhim rol o'ynaydi. Ba'zan professional yaxshiroq ish qila oladi va qimmat xatolardan qochadi. Nihoyat, ba'zi vazifalar o'z-o'zidan yoqimsiz yoki xavfli bo'ladi, shuning uchun ularni autsorsing qilish ko'p odamlar uchun mantiqiy.

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several reasons why many people opt for paid services rather than doing things themselves, as we can see in the first photo.
Primarily, the most obvious reason is time constraints. In today's fast-paced world, many people are extremely busy with work, family responsibilities, and other commitments. Hiring a professional saves them valuable time that they can spend on more important or enjoyable activities.
Additionally, professionals bring expertise and experience that most ordinary people lack. Whether it's cleaning, plumbing, or car repair, a trained professional will typically do a better job in less time. The quality of the result is usually higher.
Furthermore, some tasks can be physically demanding or even risky for untrained individuals. Paying for a service provides peace of mind and ensures the job is done safely and correctly. As they say, "Time is money", and sometimes it makes more sense to pay someone else to do the work.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ko'pchilikning o'z ishlarni o'zi qilishdan ko'ra pullik xizmatlarni tanlashiga bir nechta sabablar bor, buni birinchi suratda ko'rishimiz mumkin.

Asosan, eng aniq sabab - vaqt cheklovlari. Bugungi tez sur'atlar bilan rivojlanayotgan dunyoda ko'pchilik ish, oilaviy majburiyatlar va boshqa vazifalar bilan juda band. Mutaxassisni yollash ularga qimmatli vaqtni tejaydi, ular bu vaqtni muhimroq yoki yoqimliroq mashg'ulotlarga sarflashlari mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, mutaxassislar ko'pchilik oddiy odamlarda bo'lmagan tajriba va malakaga ega. Farqi yo'q, uyni tozalash, santexnika yoki avtomobil ta'miri bo'ladimi, o'qitilgan mutaxassis odatda ishni qisqa vaqt ichida yaxshiroq bajaradi. Natijaning sifati odatda yuqori bo'ladi.

Bundan tashqari, ba'zi vazifalar jismonan og'ir yoki hatto tayyorgarliksiz odamlar uchun xavfli bo'lishi mumkin. Xizmat uchun pul to'lash xotirjamlikni ta'minlaydi va ishning xavfsiz va to'g'ri bajarilishini kafolatlaydi. Aytishlaricha, "Vaqt - pul", va ba'zida ishni boshqa birovga to'lash mantiqan to'g'riroq bo'ladi.

questions.prompt: Describe a time when you changed your opinion about something.
questions.sampleA1:
I... I think... before, I no like football.

Now, I like. My friend like.
questions.sampleA2:
I used to not like coffee.

I thought it was bad.

But then I tried it with sugar and milk, and I liked it.

questions.sampleB1:
I used to think that online learning wasn't very good.

I thought it was much better to be in a classroom with a teacher.

However, during the pandemic, I had to study online, and I realised it can be really effective.

For example, I could learn at my own pace, and there were lots of resources available.

So, now I think online learning is a good option, too.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so I'd like to talk about a time when I completely changed my mind about online learning. Back when I was at school, I was convinced that studying online was a total waste of time. I firmly believed that you could only learn properly in a classroom, sitting face to face with a teacher who could keep an eye on you. To be honest, I looked down on it and saw it as an excuse for people to be lazy. What made me change my tune was the pandemic. Almost overnight, all my classes moved online, and I had no choice but to give it a proper go. Much to my surprise, I found I could learn at my own pace, pause the lessons, and go over anything I hadn't grasped. On top of that, there was a wealth of free resources at my fingertips — YouTube tutorials, online courses, you name it. Little by little, I came round to the idea, and now I genuinely think it was one of the best things to come out of that whole period. As for why some people chop and change their opinions so often, I suppose it varies. Some folks are easily swayed by whatever they see on social media and don't really think things through for themselves. That said, I don't think changing your mind is always a bad thing. Ultimately, being willing to look at fresh evidence and admit you were wrong is a real sign of maturity, not weakness.

bulletPoints: Describe a time when you changed your opinion about something.
Why do some people tend to change their opinions very often?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time I changed my opinion:
I used to believe that social media was a complete waste of time and had no real value. I saw it as purely a distraction that stopped people from being productive. This was my firmly held view for several years during my school days.
What made me change my mind:
What fundamentally changed my perspective was when I started using social media for educational purposes. I discovered that platforms like YouTube and Telegram had incredibly valuable learning communities and free courses. I also saw how small businesses used Instagram to reach customers and how people connected across borders. This made me realise that social media is just a tool — its value depends entirely on how you use it.
Why some people change opinions often:
I think some people change their opinions frequently because they are easily influenced by others or by what they see in the media. They may lack strong convictions or haven't done enough research to form a solid viewpoint. However, changing one's mind can also be a sign of intellectual maturity — being open to new evidence and different perspectives is a strength, not a weakness. As they say, "The measure of intelligence is the ability to change".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Fikrimni o'zgartirgan vaqt:

Men ilgari ijtimoiy tarmoqlar vaqtni mutlaqo bekorga sarflash va hech qanday real qiymatga ega emas deb hisoblardim. Men uni odamlarni unumli bo'lishdan to'xtatadigan shunchaki chalg'ituvchi narsa deb bilardim. Bu mening maktab yillarimda bir necha yil davomida qat'iy ushlagan nuqtai nazarim edi.

Fikrimni o'zgartirgan narsa:

Mening nuqtai nazarimni tubdan o'zgartirgan narsa, ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan ta'lim maqsadlarida foydalana boshlaganim bo'ldi. Men YouTube va Telegram kabi platformalarda juda qimmatli o'quv hamjamiyatlari va bepul kurslar borligini aniqladim. Shuningdek, kichik bizneslar Instagramdan mijozlarga yetib borish uchun qanday foydalanishini va odamlar chegaralar bo'ylab qanday bog'lanishini ko'rdim. Bu menga ijtimoiy tarmoqlar shunchaki vosita ekanligini anglatdi — uning qiymati butunlay undan qanday foydalanishingizga bog'liq.

Nima uchun ba'zi odamlar tez-tez fikrini o'zgartiradi:

Menimcha, ba'zi odamlar o'z fikrlarini tez-tez o'zgartiradilar, chunki ularga boshqalar yoki ommaviy axborot vositalarida ko'rgan narsalari oson ta'sir qiladi. Ularda kuchli e'tiqodlar yetishmasligi yoki mustahkam nuqtai nazarni shakllantirish uchun yetarli tadqiqotlar olib bormagan bo'lishi mumkin. Biroq, fikrni o'zgartirish aqliy yetuklik belgisi ham bo'lishi mumkin — yangi dalillarga va turli nuqtai nazarlarga ochiq bo'lish zaiflik emas, balki kuchdir. Aytishlaricha, "Aqlning o'lchovi - o'zgarish qobiliyatidir".

questions.prompt: Traditional crafts and skills are no longer important in the modern world.
questions.sampleA1: Crafts? I don't know. Maybe no. I like phone.
questions.sampleA2: I think crafts are okay. My grandma likes crafts, and she makes things. But I don't like them so much because they are slow. I like video games more.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think traditional crafts are still important, but maybe not as important as before. For example, my mom likes to knit, and she makes nice things. However, a lot of people buy things from shops because it's easier and faster. In my opinion, it's good to keep the old skills alive, but it's also important to have modern things.
questions.sampleB2: Well, this is a really interesting statement, and I can honestly see both sides of the argument. On the one hand, I understand why some people would agree. In this day and age, machines can churn out products far more cheaply and quickly than any craftsman, so traditional skills like weaving or pottery can seem a bit outdated. A lot of young people simply aren't drawn to them, because they'd rather chase better-paid careers in tech or business. Having said that, I personally have to disagree with the statement. The way I see it, traditional crafts are worth their weight in gold, because they keep our cultural heritage alive and connect us to our roots. Once these skills die out, they're gone for good, and that would be a real shame. What's more, there's actually been a growing appreciation for handmade goods lately — people are fed up with cheap, mass-produced items and are willing to pay a premium for something unique. On top of that, these crafts can provide a decent livelihood for whole communities, especially in rural areas where jobs are thin on the ground. So when all is said and done, while I admit that traditional crafts have taken a back seat in some ways, I firmly believe they still have a vital part to play. A society that turns its back on its heritage risks losing a huge part of what makes it unique, and that, in my view, is a price we simply shouldn't be willing to pay.

for: Modern technology makes production faster and cheaper.
Young people today show little interest in learning old skills.

against: Traditional crafts preserve unique cultural identity and heritage.
They can create sustainable and meaningful job opportunities.
They connect us to our history and give a sense of pride.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a thought-provoking statement that touches on the tension between modernity and tradition.
Those who agree that traditional crafts are no longer important point out that modern technology has made production faster, cheaper, and more efficient. Why spend days weaving a carpet by hand when a machine can produce one in hours? Moreover, young people today show relatively little interest in learning old skills — they're more drawn to digital careers and modern professions. Additionally, machines produce more consistent and higher-quality items, reducing human error and waste.
However, I believe the opposing arguments are even stronger. Traditional crafts are not just about making objects — they preserve cultural identity and heritage. Every handwoven fabric, every piece of pottery tells a story about a community's history and values. Furthermore, these crafts can create sustainable and meaningful employment, particularly in rural areas where factory jobs may not exist. They also connect us to our roots and give people a deep sense of pride in their culture.
Personally, I disagree with the statement. Traditional crafts and modern technology should coexist. We can use technology to preserve and promote these skills rather than replace them. As they say, "A nation's culture resides in the hearts and in the soul of its people".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu zamonaviylik va an'ana o'rtasidagi ziddiyatga tegishli bo'lgan o'ylantiradigan fikr.

An'anaviy hunarmandchilik endi muhim emas deb hisoblaydiganlar, zamonaviy texnologiya ishlab chiqarishni tezroq, arzonroq va samaraliroq qilganini ta'kidlashadi. Mashina bir necha soat ichida gilam to'qishi mumkin bo'lsa, nega uni qo'lda to'qish uchun kunlar sarflash kerak? Bundan tashqari, bugungi yoshlar eski hunarlarni o'rganishga nisbatan unchalik qiziqish bildirmayapti — ularni ko'proq raqamli kasblar va zamonaviy sohalar jalb qilmoqda. Qolaversa, mashinalar inson xatolarini va chiqindilarni kamaytirib, yanada barqaror va yuqori sifatli mahsulotlar ishlab chiqaradi.

Biroq, menimcha, qarama-qarshi dalillar yanada kuchliroq. An'anaviy hunarmandchilik faqatgina buyumlar yasash haqida emas — ular madaniy o'zlikni va merosni saqlaydi. Har bir qo'lda to'qilgan mato, har bir kulolchilik buyumi jamiyat tarixidan va qadriyatlaridan hikoya qiladi. Bundan tashqari, bu hunarmandchilik, ayniqsa zavod ishlari mavjud bo'lmagan qishloq joylarda, barqaror va mazmunli ish bilan ta'minlash imkoniyatini yaratishi mumkin. Ular, shuningdek, bizni ildizlarimizga bog'laydi va odamlarga o'z madaniyatidan chuqur faxrlanish hissini beradi.

Shaxsan men bu fikrga qo'shilmayman. An'anaviy hunarmandchilik va zamonaviy texnologiya birga yashashi kerak. Biz texnologiyadan bu hunarlarni almashtirish o'rniga, ularni saqlash va targ'ib qilish uchun foydalanishimiz mumkin. Aytishlaricha, "Millatning madaniyati uning xalqining yuragida va ruhida yashaydi".
